preserved_objections.basis: The proposed mechanism of "low rubber-filler interaction and rigidity of crosslink network" directly contradicts established elastomer science where optimal mechanical properties require balanced filler-rubber interaction and crosslink density. The cited evidence on fatigue life analysis of laminated elastomeric bearing pads demonstrates that excessive rigidity leads to premature crack propagation under cyclic loading.

No boundary conditions are specified, making the proposal completely untestable. Bridge bearing pads operate under extreme environmental conditions (temperature cycling, UV exposure, chemical exposure, variable loads) that would critically affect the proposed modification, yet none are addressed or controlled for in the proposal.

The evidence provided includes research on hydrogenated natural rubber, seismic damage indices, and fatigue life analysis, none of which support the specific claim about N220 carbon filler in a semi-efficient vulcanization system improving 75-year equivalent aging performance. The organic electrochemical transistor paper is entirely irrelevant to elastomeric bridge bearing technology.

The proposal fails to demonstrate any advantage over the baseline. The predicted effects (improved tensile properties, reduced compression set) are standard industry improvements, not breakthroughs. The evidence on seismic damage indices specifically shows that elastomeric pad performance degrades over time regardless of minor compound modifications.

The proposed modification cannot be implemented in real-world manufacturing. N220 carbon filler requires precise dispersion and mixing protocols that are incompatible with large-scale production of bridge bearing pads. The semi-efficient vulcanization system would require exact temperature and time controls that are impossible to maintain consistently across the large cross-sections of industrial bearing pads.

The testable prediction of compression set and tensile strength after "75-year equivalent aging" is scientifically meaningless. There is no validated accelerated aging protocol that can accurately predict 75-year performance, and the proposal fails to specify the aging conditions, making the prediction impossible to verify.
